title: The First Sitting
summary: The Constituent Assembly meets for the first time; Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha takes the Chair as temporary Chairman.

title: The Assembly Makes Its Rules
summary: The Assembly settles the process for choosing its permanent President and begins framing its own procedure.

title: The Objectives Resolution
summary: Jawaharlal Nehru moves the Objectives Resolution, setting out the Assembly’s early constitutional aims.

title: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
summary: Opening presiding figure of the Assembly and principal voice of the first sitting.

title: J. B. Kripalani
summary: Important early procedural voice, including election procedure and the Rules Committee.

title: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Moved the Objectives Resolution and articulated the Assembly’s early constitutional aims.

title: Rules & Procedure
summary: How the Assembly created legitimate procedures for its own work before drafting the Constitution.

title: Objectives Resolution
summary: Popular sovereignty, independence, justice, equality and safeguards as an early constitutional programme.

title: Language
summary: Language questions appeared in the Assembly from its first procedural sittings.

title: Institution-building
summary: The Assembly had to establish its offices, rules, chair and procedures while beginning constitution-making.

title: Preamble
summary: The Objectives Resolution is a major antecedent for the political ideals later expressed in the Preamble.

title: Article 1 — Union and Territory
summary: The Objectives Resolution framed the territorial and political community that later took constitutional form.

title: Fundamental Rights
summary: Justice, equality, freedoms and safeguards in the Objectives Resolution anticipate later rights debates.

title: Official Record — 11 December 1946
summary: Election of Dr. Rajendra Prasad as permanent Chairman.

title: Official Record — 12 December 1946
summary: Objectives Resolution discussion postponed to allow members more time.
